blocks.title: Discover
blocks.text: A linked-list node holds a value plus one or more links to neighbouring nodes, rather than occupying an indexed fixed-size array slot.

blocks.title: Trace
blocks.text: C# LinkedList<T> is doubly linked: nodes expose Previous and Next; AddAfter inserts relative to an existing node.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: To insert B between A and C, change logical links to A↔B↔C. The operation differs from shifting array elements.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain the trace
blocks.text: New order A,X,B. The inserted node links between A and B.

blocks.title: Explain the trace
blocks.text: P,R remain. After deletion P and R are adjacent logical neighbours.

Choose the response that best addresses this independent task: FOUNDATION · Q1/3 Draw the logical next-links in HEAD→3→6→NULL after inserting 4 after 3. [6]
questions.answer: WORKED MODEL ANSWER 3.next becomes 4 [2], 4.next=6 [2], final HEAD→3→4→6→NULL [2].
options: WORKED MODEL ANSWER 3.next becomes 4 [2], 4.next=6 [2], final HEAD→3→4→6→NULL [2].
WORKED MODEL ANSWER var l=new LinkedList<int>(); [1]; l.AddLast(2); l.AddLast(4); [2]; l.AddAfter(l.First!,3); [3].
WORKED MODEL ANSWER List indexed access O(1) [2], insertion shifts subsequent values O(n) [1]; linked-list insertion with node reference O(1) links [2], finding node may take O(n) [1].
questions.feedback: WORKED MODEL ANSWER 3.next becomes 4 [2], 4.next=6 [2], final HEAD→3→4→6→NULL [2].
